text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hassan says in message to Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali: "We must remain faithful to commitments on which we founded the Arab Maghreb Union". - Andre Azoulay,
economic adviser to King Hassan, tells Euromoney capital markets and investment forum held in Rabat of need to develop capital markets to help Moroccan companies compete in the new free trade zone.
- Morocco's economic thinktank Centre Marocain de Conjoncture says economic pickup blocked by a tight budget policy.
- Unemployment in cities dropped by 4.3 percent in the first nine months of 1996 to 18.7 percent from 23 percent at end 1995.
- Moroccan Organisation of Human rights (OMDH) condemns French immigration bill requiring citizens to declare presence of visitors on short-term tourist visas.
- State-owned Office National des Aeroports expected to devote 1.4 billion dirhams ($152 million) to upgrade airports so that they comply with international security norms.
